# Physical second-order tests for three fixed planar cap budgets

This note gives an exact second-order test for the fixed-cap volume problem in global-support-stress.md. All variations move actual triangle vertices, all caps stay fixed, and the complete mixed body is retained. The conclusions are a strict constrained second variation for one triangle, a strictly improving two-fiber path despite its normalized first-order support stress, and the corresponding strict stability for a six-cap critical cover. These are bounded variational results, not an OC proof or counterexample.

The mechanism differs from the archived diffuse support-arc variations: the present fibers are polytopes, their facet normals move, and the cap constraints have exact rational vertex formulas.

## 1. Three fixed caps and their exact physical derivatives

Let \(T=\operatorname{conv}\{(0,0),(1,0),(0,1)\}\), of area \(1/2\). Fix
\[
H_0=\{x+y\le2/3\},\qquad
H_1=\{x\ge1/3\},\qquad H_2=\{y\ge1/3\}.
\tag{1}
\]
They cover the entire plane: if neither of the last two contains a point, its coordinate sum is less than \(2/3\). Each cuts area \(2/9\) from \(T\).

Consider nearby triangles with labeled vertices \(v_j=(x_j,y_j)\), \(j=0,1,2\), preserving their positive orientation. Write \(z=(x_0,y_0,x_1,y_1,x_2,y_2)\) and
\[
A(z)=\tfrac12\det
\begin{pmatrix}1&x_0&y_0\\1&x_1&y_1\\1&x_2&y_2\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Let the three affine cap margins be
\[
f_0(x,y)=2/3-x-y,\quad f_1(x,y)=x-1/3,\quad f_2(x,y)=y-1/3,
\]
and \(c_{ij}=f_i(v_j)\). Near \(T\), cap \(i\) strictly includes only vertex \(i\). Its exact area is
\[
F_i(z)=A(z)\frac{c_{ii}^{\,2}}
{(c_{ii}-c_{ij})(c_{ii}-c_{ik})},\qquad\{j,k\}=\{0,1,2\}\setminus\{i\}.
\tag{2}
\]
This follows by the two edge-intersection ratios; all denominators stay positive. Thus the physical mass functions are smooth on this actual open vertex chamber.

At \(z_*=(0,0,1,0,0,1)\), their gradient matrix is
\[
G=\begin{pmatrix}\nabla F_0\\\nabla F_1\\\nabla F_2\end{pmatrix}
=\frac19
\begin{pmatrix}
-4&-4&0&-2&-2&0\\
0&-2&4&0&2&2\\
-2&0&2&2&0&4
\end{pmatrix}.
\tag{3}
\]
In particular
\[
\nabla A=\tfrac34(\nabla F_0+\nabla F_1+\nabla F_2).
\tag{4}
\]
The objective multiplier is one and all cap multipliers are \(3/4\).

The same stress is visible in the finite support cone from global-support-stress.md. On each original edge, the sum of its lengths lying in the three open caps is \(4/3\) times the edge length. Multiplication by \(3/4\) gives the ordinary area derivative. No cap plane coincides with an edge. Equation (4) is stronger for this example: it also retains all six physical vertex directions, including moving facet normals.

## 2. Strict second-order stability on the one-triangle critical tangent

Let \(\mathscr L=A-\tfrac34\sum_iF_i\). Every \(\delta\in\ker G\) has the unique form
\[
\delta=(p/2-q/2+r,\ -p-r,\ -p/2-q/2-r,\ p,\ q,\ r).
\tag{5}
\]
Differentiating the exact rational formulas (2) gives
\[
D^2\mathscr L(z_*)[\delta,\delta]
=-\frac18\left[(p+q+r)^2+2(p-q)^2+3r^2\right].
\tag{6}
\]
The right side is strictly negative unless \(\delta=0\). For reproducibility, the matrix in coordinates \((p,q,r)\) is
\[
\frac18\begin{pmatrix}-3&1&-1\\1&-3&-1\\-1&-1&-4\end{pmatrix}.
\]

Consequently, for any actual \(C^2\) path of triangles with
\[
F_i(z(t))\le2/9,\qquad z(0)=z_*,\qquad z'(0)=\delta\in\ker G,
\]
the one-sided second derivative satisfies
\[
A''(0)\le-\frac18\left[(p+q+r)^2+2(p-q)^2+3r^2\right].
\tag{7}
\]
Indeed \(F_i'(0)=0\), so each \(F_i''(0)\le0\). Equation (4) cancels the path acceleration from the Lagrangian second derivative. This proves (7) without pretending that an arbitrary straight vertex path preserves the cap budgets.

There is also a local quadratic area loss: some \(c,\varepsilon>0\) satisfy
\[
A(z)\le\tfrac12-c\|z-z_*\|^2
\tag{8}
\]
for all feasible triangles in \(\|z-z_*\|<\varepsilon\). Here is a compact proof, which does not claim an explicit optimal \(c\). If (8) failed, take feasible \(z_\ell=z_*+t_\ell d_\ell\), \(t_\ell\downarrow0\), \(\|d_\ell\|=1\), with \(A(z_\ell)\ge1/2-t_\ell^2/\ell\). Feasibility gives \(Gd_\ell\le O(t_\ell)\), while the area expansion and (4) give \(\sum_i(Gd_\ell)_i\ge-O(t_\ell)\). After a subsequence, the limiting unit vector lies in \(\ker G\). Since \(\nabla\mathscr L(z_*)=0\), (6) and Taylor expansion give
\[
A(z_\ell)-\tfrac12
\le\mathscr L(z_\ell)-\mathscr L(z_*)
\le-c_0t_\ell^2
\]
for some \(c_0>0\), a contradiction. This is a triangle-parameter stability result, not a claim about arbitrary Hausdorff perturbations of convex bodies.

## 3. Two adjacent fibers satisfy the same first stress but admit a strict improvement

Put two copies of \(T\) at integer bases \(0,1\). Their convex hull has precisely these two integer fibers; the total mixed area is one. Make each cap (1) cylindrical in the base coordinate. The caps cover all of \(\{0,1\}\times\mathbb R^2\), each has mass \(4/9\), and summing (4) over the two fibers gives the same global multiplier vector
\[
\lambda_0=\lambda_1=\lambda_2=3/4.
\]
There is no active compatibility inequality between the two exposed fibers. Thus the normalized first-order support stress is satisfied with zero compatibility stress.

Let
\[
q=t^2/3,\qquad L=1+7t^2/18,\qquad 0<t\le1/10,
\]
and replace the two actual fibers by
\[
T_\pm(t)=\operatorname{conv}\{(q\pm t,q\pm t),(L,0),(0,L)\}.
\tag{9}
\]
The first velocities of their first vertices are opposite. By (3), every total cap derivative vanishes, as does the total area derivative. The changes \(q\) and \(L-1\) are a common physical acceleration of order \(t^2\).

All triangles remain positively oriented, and each cap keeps its same unique included vertex: \(q+t<1/3<L\), \(L>2/3\), and \(L-2(q+t)>0\). Their convex hull over bases \(0,1\) is a full-dimensional actual body, with exactly the two displayed integer fibers.

The total mixed area is exactly
\[
M(t)=L(L-2q)
=1+\frac{t^2}{9}-\frac{35t^4}{324}>1.
\tag{10}
\]
The two coordinate caps have the same mass \(C_1(t)=C_2(t)\). Their exact values and the first cap's value follow directly by summing (2):
\[
C_0(t)=\sum_{\sigma=\pm1}
\frac{L(2/3-2(q+\sigma t))^2}{2(L-2(q+\sigma t))},
\]
\[
C_1(t)=C_2(t)=\sum_{\sigma=\pm1}
\frac{(L-2(q+\sigma t))(L-1/3)^2}{2(L-q-\sigma t)}.
\tag{11}
\]
In particular,
\[
\frac49-C_0(t)=
\frac{4t^2(35t^6-1303t^4-2892t^2+108)}
{9(5t^2-36t-18)(5t^2+36t-18)}>0,
\tag{12}
\]
\[
\frac49-C_1(t)=
\frac{t^2(245t^6+36120t^4+105948t^2+7776)}
{324(t^2-18t+18)(t^2+18t+18)}>0.
\tag{13}
\]
Both denominator products are positive on \(0<t\le1/10\). For (12), setting \(\tau=t^2\le1/100\) bounds its polynomial below by
\[
108-2892/100-1303/10000=789497/10000>0.
\]
Every coefficient in the numerator polynomial of (13) is positive. Thus (9) strictly increases total volume and strictly decreases every fixed cap mass, throughout an explicit rational interval.

The leading terms show the second-order mechanism:
\[
M(t)=1+t^2/9+O(t^4),\quad
C_0(t)=4/9-4t^2/27+O(t^4),\quad
C_{1,2}(t)=4/9-2t^2/27+O(t^4).
\]
For the opposite vertex velocity \(v=(1,1,0,0,0,0)\), one triangle has \(D^2\mathscr L[v,v]=1/3\). Therefore the aggregate critical direction \((v,-v)\) has positive Lagrangian second variation \(2/3\), although a single triangle's constrained critical tangent has the negative form (6). The total cap constraints allow first-order changes in one fiber to be canceled by those in the other. The common acceleration then makes the gain feasible simultaneously for all three caps.

At \(t=1/10\), one exact witness is
\[
M=648713/648000,\qquad
C_0=685451117/1546212500,\qquad
C_1=C_2=923058069551/2080858248000.
\]
No numerical optimization is used.

## 4. A critical six-cap calibration with strict physical stability

For comparison, localize one copy of each cap to each integer base. Using the margins \(f_i\) above, fix
\[
H_{0i}=\{f_i(x)-z\ge0\},\qquad
H_{1i}=\{f_i(x)+z-1\ge0\},\qquad i=0,1,2.
\tag{14}
\]
At base zero the first three cover the entire continuous plane; at base one the second three do. The opposite groups strictly exclude \(T\), because \(\max_T f_i=2/3<1\). Each cap has mass exactly \(2/9\) on the initial two-fiber body.

These budgets make the initial body an actual global fixed-cap volume maximizer over the fixed two-base support \(P=\{0,1\}\), as in the fixed-support problem of global-support-stress.md. Any competing fiber at one of these two bases has its own three cap areas at most \(2/9\), and those three caps cover the plane. At that fiber's ordinary centroid, at least one contains the centroid and thus at least a \(\Gamma_2=4/9\) fraction of its area. Its area is therefore at most \(1/2\), and the total is at most one.

These six caps are at the actual initial mixed depth value: the own centroid of either fiber has depth \(2/9\); base tilts can isolate that fiber and realize its ordinary simplex cap, giving the matching upper bound at every candidate.

For nearby triangle fibers the opposite groups remain strictly empty. A critical \(C^2\) feasible path thus has each individual fiber velocity in \(\ker G\). Applying (7) twice gives the exact negative sum of the two quadratic forms. In particular any nonzero physical first velocity strictly decreases total area to second order, and (8) yields local quadratic rigidity in the twelve vertex coordinates.

The comparison of Sections 3 and 4 is the geometric content of the test: shared cap budgets and independently localized critical cap budgets have different second-order feasible directions even when their normalized first-order cap weights agree.

## 5. Scope

The three cylindrical budgets of Section 3 are larger than the true critical depth budget of the initial two-fiber body. That example therefore does not refute any condition asserted only at an attained depth minimizer. It proves that first-order global support stress, even with positive normalized multipliers and a full-space cap cover, does not replace the physical second-order optimality requirement.

The six-cap example supplies an actual critical-cover maximizer and an explicit strictly negative constrained quadratic form. Neither example asserts an arbitrary higher-dimensional mixed-volume sign, a mass allocation across arbitrary cap groups, or a global OC conclusion.
